title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-31
content:
Morning dump - quick status and running list. Informal notes, triage items, perf experiments.

Today
- Focus: KV-cache correctness + perf regression seen in canary (2026-03-30 22:14 UTC).
- Blockers: flaky kernel fallback on A100s when sequence > 2048 (observed OOM trace).

Recent context / recap
- Canary 2026-03-30 rolled model v2.3.1 with kernel selector change (PR GH-PR-889). Average latency looks fine on short seqs but P95 jumped ~18% on long seqs.
- Error spike: ~0.8% requests hit fallback path, increased CPU usage on host. Root cause unknown; hypothesis: kernel memory estimator undercounts activation size for quantized attention.

Immediate triage checklist
- [ ] Reproduce locally with seq=4096 on A100-80GB image (use mig off). Use workload-sim: ./tools/loadgen --model redwood/gptx-8b --seq 4096 --batch 1 --quant 4bit
- [ ] Capture full dmesg + nvml logs when kernel fallback occurs
- [ ] Run memprof on runtime to check per-layer allocation (memprof branch: debug/memprof)
- [ ] Roll back selector to v2.3.0 on one canary shard to confirm regression source (depends on GH-PR-889 revert)
- [ ] Add assertion to kernel selector: predicted_needed >= observed_peak_estimate (cheap check)

Perf TODOs (short term)
- Add microbenchmark for KV cache lookup hot path (latency and allocation). Put results in confluence perf page.
- Tune continuous batching parameters: target_batch_ewma alpha from 0.2 -> 0.1 for long-tail workloads. Observe effect on tail latency.
- Evaluate quantization profile used for 8-bit GEMM (last tuned Nov 2025). Try alternative rounding mode for attention kernels.

Kernel notes / experiments
- Observed kernel ATAttn_v3 has a corner-case when seq_len % 128 != 0 -> temp buffer alignment leads to extra pages. Need to validate page-aligned allocator.
- Experiment: use posix_memalign(, 4096) for temp buffers in attention and measure TLB pressure.
- If alignment fixes spike, make alignment configurable behind env var REDWOOD_KERN_TMP_ALIGN to avoid global rebuilds.

Quick commands and snippets
- reproduce locally:
  docker run --gpus all -it --rm redwood/runtime:test-2026-03-30 \n    /bin/bash -c "./bin/serve --model redwood/gptx-8b --seq 4096 --quant 4bit --log-level debug > /tmp/serve.log 2>&1"
- capture nvml:
  python tools/nvml_dump.py --interval 0.5 --duration 300 --out /tmp/nvml.json
- memprof run:
  git checkout debug/memprof && bazel build //runtime:memprof && ./bazel-bin/runtime/memprof --target pid

Notes for PR and rollout
- If fix is kernel selector param tweak, prefer a canary config override (routing rule) instead of code revert so customers on Dedicated can opt-in.
- Update release notes with details: P95 regression, mitigations, and follow-up plan. Add to product-facing incident templated doc if user-facing impact > 0.5%.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Why did only long seq samples regress? Could be rare branch in attention kernel or different memory allocation pattern. Need traces.
- Check if Dedicated customers reported anomalies (CS pinged on 2026-03-31). Follow-up with account Mgr Sally R.

Misc TODOs (personal)
- [ ] Sync with Priya on rollout plan (30m)
- [ ] Write up short runbook snippet for kernel fallback (15m)
- [ ] Add unit tests for alignment case (couple hours)

Reference links / tickets
- JIRA: JIRA-RT-4123 (canary regression)
- GH: GH-PR-889 (kernel selector change)
- Confluence perf page: confluence://perf-runbook/serve-optimizations

Random notes (brain dump)
- Could cache predicted_needed sizes per model family instead of computing every request to save cycles — store in small LRU with TTL 10m.
- Consider instrumenting a small bloom-filter style fast check for large-seq requests to skip expensive estimator if seen recently.

End of day plan
- Repro + memprof by EOD. If repro: push hotfix branch with selector guard and run canary. If not repro: collect more logs and open deeper trace with SRE.

-- Jordan
(quick scratchpad, will move important items to GH issues / JIRA later)
